from pysat.solvers import Glucose4
from pysat.card import CardEnc, EncType
from itertools import combinations

G = 24
W = 8
K = 8  # groups per week
S = 3  # group size

# Variables: x[w][p][g] = 1 if player p is in group g in week w
var = {}
next_var = 1
for w in range(W):
    for p in range(G):
        for g in range(K):
            var[(w,p,g)] = next_var
            next_var += 1

# same[w][p][q] = 1 if p,q in same group in week w (p<q)
# We'll add auxiliary only when needed via clauses.
# Instead use direct: for each pair (p,q), sum over weeks of "in same group" <=1.
# "in same group week w" = OR over g of (x[w,p,g] AND x[w,q,g]).
# Define y[w,p,q] aux variable
y = {}
for w in range(W):
    for p,q in combinations(range(G),2):
        y[(w,p,q)] = next_var
        next_var += 1

clauses = []

# Each player in exactly one group per week
for w in range(W):
    for p in range(G):
        vars_pg = [var[(w,p,g)] for g in range(K)]
        # at least one
        clauses.append(vars_pg[:])
        # at most one
        for a,b in combinations(vars_pg,2):
            clauses.append([-a,-b])

# Each group has exactly 3 players per week (at most/at least)
# Using sequential encoding via CardEnc
top_id = [next_var-1]
def new_vars(n):
    res = list(range(top_id[0]+1, top_id[0]+1+n))
    top_id[0] += n
    return res

for w in range(W):
    for g in range(K):
        lits = [var[(w,p,g)] for p in range(G)]
        # exactly 3
        cnf_eq = CardEnc.equals(lits=lits, bound=3, top_id=top_id[0], encoding=EncType.seqcounter)
        if cnf_eq.nv > top_id[0]:
            top_id[0] = cnf_eq.nv
        clauses.extend(cnf_eq.clauses)

# y[w,p,q] definition: y iff exists g with x[w,p,g] AND x[w,q,g]
# For each g: (x[w,p,g] AND x[w,q,g]) -> y[w,p,q]
# i.e., -x[w,p,g] OR -x[w,q,g] OR y
# And y -> OR_g (x[w,p,g] AND x[w,q,g])
# Actually we only need: if p,q in same group week w, then y=1. Then constraint sum y <= 1 over w.
# We don't need reverse direction. So just the forward implication.
for w in range(W):
    for p,q in combinations(range(G),2):
        yv = y[(w,p,q)]
        for g in range(K):
            clauses.append([-var[(w,p,g)], -var[(w,q,g)], yv])

# At most one week per pair
for p,q in combinations(range(G),2):
    lits = [y[(w,p,q)] for w in range(W)]
    # at most 1
    for a,b in combinations(lits,2):
        clauses.append([-a,-b])

print("vars:", top_id[0], "clauses:", len(clauses))

solver = Glucose4()
for c in clauses:
    solver.add_clause(c)

# Symmetry breaking: week 0 fix assignment
# Players 0,1,2 -> group 0; 3,4,5 -> group 1; ...; 21,22,23 -> group 7
for i in range(G):
    g = i // 3
    solver.add_clause([var[(0,i,g)]])

# Week 1: player 0 in group 0
solver.add_clause([var[(1,0,0)]])

import time
t=time.time()
res = solver.solve()
print("solve:", res, time.time()-t)
if res:
    model = set(solver.get_model())
    out = []
    for w in range(W):
        for p in range(G):
            for g in range(K):
                if var[(w,p,g)] in model:
                    out.append(g)
                    break
    print(out)
